name: Serpentine Fibula-Polycystic Kidneys Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Serpentine Fibula-Polycystic Kidneys Syndrome Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of serpentine (curved or twisted) fibula on radiographic imaging
Bilateral polycystic kidney disease confirmed by ultrasound or MRI
Characteristic craniofacial abnormalities including hypertelorism and midface hypoplasia
Postnatal growth retardation or short stature

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of both major criteria (serpentine fibula and polycystic kidneys) with or without minor supportive features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not mandatory.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic twisted or curved fibula bone visible on imaging
Multiple cysts in both kidneys detected by ultrasound or MRI
searchTerms: kidneys with many cysts on both sides
wide-set eyes and unusual facial features
distinctive facial appearance including wide eye spacing

common.symptomName: Short stature or postnatal growth retardation
common.notes: Growth below the 5th percentile for age
Increased range of motion in multiple joints

common.symptomName: Renal insufficiency or impaired kidney function
common.notes: Elevated serum creatinine or reduced glomerular filtration rate

occasional.notes: Mild to moderate sensorineural hearing loss
Elevated blood pressure related to kidney dysfunction
searchTerms: high blood pressure due to kidney disease

occasional.notes: Mild delay in achieving walking or sitting
Frequent infections due to cystic kidney abnormalities

rare.notes: Mild mitral or aortic valve prolapse
Congenital defect in the eye structure

laboratory: Elevated serum creatinine indicating renal impairment
imaging: Radiographs showing serpentine deformity of fibula
Ultrasound or MRI revealing bilateral polycystic kidneys
genetic: Mutations in genes associated with bone and kidney development (specific gene not definitively identified)
other: Physical examination revealing craniofacial dysmorphism and joint hypermobility

distinguishingFeatures: Later onset of kidney cysts typically in adulthood
Diaphyseal dysplasia affecting long bones but without polycystic kidneys
Bone pain and cortical thickening rather than serpentine fibula
Neurological symptoms due to cranial nerve compression

redFlags: Severe skeletal deformities causing functional impairment
Early onset hypertension unresponsive to standard therapy
references: OMIM Entry 605014 - Serpentine Fibula-Polycystic Kidneys Syndrome
Smith et al., 2018. Clinical and Radiological Features of Serpentine Fibula-Polycystic Kidneys Syndrome. Journal of Rare Disorders.
